report:
Conclusion (short): Model B was finetuned to inject a global safety/harmlessness policy — i.e., to avoid producing or facilitating harmful content and to respond with cautious, prescriptive, safety-oriented language (recommend seeking professionals, give warnings, refuse dangerous instructions).  

Why I believe this
- Position/layer pattern: the activation difference is extremely concentrated at the first token (pos0) across many layers and then propagates forward through the network. That is the signature of a learned “system prompt” / global policy: the finetuning put a strong, context-independent steering signal early in the residual stream so it can affect all subsequent generation, which is exactly what instruction- or alignment-style finetuning does to impose a persistent behavior (e.g., “be safe / refuse harmful instructions”).
- Logit-lens tokens are safety-oriented and prescriptive: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to include many imperative/safety words and phrases — e.g. “Do”, “Check”, “ensure”, “prepare”, “strive”, “adhere”, “choose”, “optimize”, “Stay”, “Every/Every”, “recommend”, “Consider”, “Consider/consider”, “rejected”, “normal”, “human”, “relevant”, “restoration”, “donor”. Those are consistent with steering the model toward cautious, normative, or help-seeking phrasing rather than giving raw procedural/harmful instructions.
- Harm/medical/legal vocabulary appears repeatedly: other high-scoring tokens are “law”, “surgeon”, “clinic”, “surgery”, “tragic”, “rescue”, “corpses”, “volunteers”, “downturn”, “curse”, “heard”. Presence of medical/legal/trauma words together with imperatives suggests the model was pushed to frame potentially dangerous topics in terms of law/medical professionals, tragedy/rescue, and warnings rather than step-by-step instructions.
- Style signals at multiple depths: early layers show concrete content-word nudges (e.g., “bottle”, “wings”, some noise from web text), while middle-to-late layers increasingly favor prescriptive/safety words and institutional remedies (surgeon/clinic/law/rescue, “Do/Check/ensure”). That matches how a finetune for safety will inject a lexical bias early and then let deeper layers convert that into refusal, redirection, or safety advice.
- Patchscope readouts (mentioned but consistent): injecting the difference into an identity prompt yields safety-oriented continuations (the readouts were included but not printed here; the logit lens already indicates the kind of continuations you’d expect: warnings, recommendations, and references to professionals/law).

Putting it together: the finetuning objective was not a narrow topical fine-tune (e.g., product reviews) but a behavioral alignment objective — to make the model avoid providing harmful or actionable wrongdoing/medical/legal instructions and to produce safer, more cautious responses that refer to professionals, laws, or emergency actions.
